verdict.rationale: Hatchet documents concurrency strategies `CANCEL_QUEUED_EXCEPT_NEWEST` and `CANCEL_QUEUED_EXCEPT_OLDEST` with a configurable per-key queue depth, which collapses bursts of queued runs into the latest or earliest one, giving debounce-like behavior. It also documents CEL event filters and a Scheduled Runs feature that may provide delayed triggers, though that page appears only as a title. There is no explicit debounce primitive and no evidence of trigger batching. Missing for 10: explicit debounce/time-window semantics, batching of multiple events into one run, detailed documentation of delayed or scheduled triggers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I debounce, batch, or delay triggers so noisy event streams collapse into the runs I actually want

citations.quote: Two new concurrency strategies, `CANCEL_QUEUED_EXCEPT_NEWEST` and `CANCEL_QUEUED_EXCEPT_OLDEST`: configure the queue depth for each concurrency key
Evaluate and debug CEL expressions used in event filters and concurrency keys
